A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the effects of errors on inference are not negligible, it is possible to obtain useful information from the data by using the methods described here.
, in general, the effect of inaccuracies in health and population data on the resulting disease risk estimates is not large, although there are some notable exceptions.

, for the data considered here, the effects of errors in both the health and population counts are not negligible, and that the proposed modelling approaches are able to provide a useful framework for investigating their impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of inaccurancies in the population and case counts are not trivial and that they should be taken into account when making inferences from spatial disease mapping studies.
the effects of inaccurancies in population counts are more severe than those in the disease data and, in general, should be taken into account when mapping health risks.
